properties.title: AIO Fact Check
properties.content: Question: medications that cause thrush Answer: Several medications can increase the risk of developing oral thrush, also known as oral candidiasis, a fungal infection in the mouth. Common culprits include antibiotics, corticosteroids (both inhaled and systemic), and chemotherapy drugs. Certain medications that cause dry mouth can also indirectly contribute to thrush, as saliva helps to keep the mouth clean and prevent fungal overgrowth, according to Everyday Health. Here's a more detailed look:: - Antibiotics: Antibiotics disrupt the natural balance of bacteria in the body, including the mouth, which can allow the Candida fungus to overgrow and cause thrush. - Corticosteroids: These medications, including inhaled forms used for asthma and COPD, and oral forms like prednisone, can suppress the immune system and create an environment where Candida can thrive. - Chemotherapy and other cancer medications: Cancer treatments can weaken the immune system and cause mouth sores, both of which increase the risk of thrush, according to OncoLink. - Medications that cause dry mouth: Antihistamines, antidepressants, certain medications for high blood pressure or heart failure, and some pain medications can reduce saliva production, making the mouth a more hospitable environment for Candida. - Inhaled corticosteroids: Inhalers for asthma and COPD can lead to thrush if the medication residue is not cleared from the mouth after use. - TNF inhibitors: These medications, used for autoimmune diseases, can also increase the risk of thrush. - Hormonal contraceptives: While not directly causing thrush, hormonal birth control can alter the body's hormonal balance, which can indirectly contribute to yeast infections. - Other medications: Medications like some anti-seizure drugs or certain cancer medications (like chemotherapy drugs or vinca alkaloids) can also be associated with an increased risk of oral thrush. It's important to note that many people carry the Candida fungus in their mouths without experiencing any problems. Thrush develops when something disrupts the natural balance, allowing the fungus to overgrow. If you are concerned about thrush or experience symptoms such as white, creamy lesions on the tongue or inner cheeks, consult with a healthcare professional for diagnosis and treatment.
